text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH urgency alert fired for `HOSTED-INFERENCE-EUWEST` (service: hosted-inference). Trigger: 95th latency > 1s and error-rate spike > 4%. Alert started 1766112233.

sarah (oncall): Acked. I'm on call — looking into it now. Can someone check routing + eu-west pool health? :phone:

mike_sre: I see a lot of `inference_worker` tails showing frequent `kv cache miss` and spikes in token latency. Also host cpu on pool-gpu-12 is pegged.

anya-runtime: Confirming high p95 and internal tracing shows a backlog at the batching layer. Batches are growing to 16+ and scheduling latency jumps.

incidentbot: Escalation: no primary ack within 3m, paging secondary. Secondary paged: darren-manager.

darren-manager: On my way. If primary loses comms we should fail traffic to fallback region. Any quick mitigation?

mike_sre: Two quick mitigations: 1) scale up eu-west reserved pool by +2 rtxs, 2) roll a subset of traffic to hosted-inference-us-east as fallback. I can trigger scale.

sarah (oncall): Do it. Also open a temporary on-call bridge — we need comms.

leon-devex: Starting ad-hoc Zoom bridge: https://zoom.redwood/abc123 (bridge created)

mike_sre: Running scale command now:

```
# infra api - scale dedicated pool
curl -X POST "https://infra.redwood.internal/pools/eu-west-1/scale" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"delta":2}'
```

mike_sre: And rolling 10% traffic to us-east with routing policy override:

```
# quick traffic reroute
redwoodctl routing override --service hosted-inference --from eu-west-1 --to us-east-1 --percent 10 --reason "latency spike eu-west"
```

anya-runtime: Applied canary reroute rules, telemetry shows p95 in eu-west dropping slightly but still high. us-east 10% has healthy response times ~180ms. Error rate on eu-west trending down from 5% -> 2.1% after scale.

sarah (oncall): We're getting customer reports for timeouts on webhook delivery (some retries). Triage: customers affected are on eu-west routed endpoints only. put on status page?

leon-devex: Drafting status page: "We are investigating increased latency and intermittent timeouts in eu-west-1 affecting webhook deliveries. Full mitigation in progress; traffic partially routed to fallback region." Will post in 5.

incidentbot: PagerDuty: Secondary acknowledged (darren-manager). Manager escalation resolved.

mike_sre: I restarted the batch scheduler on pool-gpu-12 (node 12a) because of a stuck worker loop: logs showed repeated `KVCache::miss -> fallback fetch` thrash. Restart command: `systemctl restart redwood-batcher` on node.

anya-runtime: After restart and scale, batching latency normalized, average queue length down ~60%, p95 eu-west now 420ms, error-rate 0.9%.

sarah (oncall): Can we remove the temporary routing after another 10m if metrics hold?

mike_sre: Yes. If stable for 15m I'll remove the 10% reroute and then scale down by 1. I'll also open a follow-up to investigate KV cache eviction tuning.

darren-manager: Thanks team. Good customer comms. Please capture impact window and affected customer list for postmortem.

leon-devex: Status posted: https://status.redwood/incident/1766112233. Notified support for customer outreach.

incidentbot: PagerDuty: Alert resolved (auto-close) — incident resolved at 1766112580.

sarah (oncall): Confirmed resolved from monitoring; closing bridge.

mike_sre: Follow-ups: (1) KV cache eviction tuning PR, (2) add a guard to prevent long batch growth under cache miss storms, (3) validate pager SMS gateway logs (we had a ~30s delay on secondary notification). I'll create tickets.

darren-manager: Assign actions and owners. I'll lead the postmortem and schedule a 1hr blameless review tomorrow 10am.

leon-devex: Copying thread to #postmortems with the incident id.

sarah (oncall): Kudos to everyone for quick mitigation. :thumbsup:

-- end of thread --
